title: Prepositions and Contractions
summary: Use de, em, a, and por with articles and learn their common contractions.

sections.heading: De + article
sections.body: The preposition **de** often means 'of' or 'from'. It contracts with articles: **de + o = do**, **de + a = da**, **de + os = dos**, **de + as = das**.

examples.pt: A chave da casa está aqui.

sections.heading: Em + article
sections.body: The preposition **em** means 'in', 'on', or 'at' for location. It contracts as **no, na, nos, nas**.

examples.en: The documents are in the drawers.

sections.heading: A and por contractions
sections.body: The preposition **a** contracts to **ao/aos** with masculine articles and creates **à/às** with feminine articles (crase). **Por** contracts to **pelo/pela/pelos/pelas**.

examples.en: I am going to the bank.

keyPoints: De + article contracts to do, da, dos, das.
Em + article contracts to no, na, nos, nas.
A + o = ao; a + a = à.
Por + article contracts to pelo, pela, pelos, pelas.

commonMistakes.note: In standard usage, destination with ir uses a/ao/à; 'vou no' is common informal speech in some regions.
